title: Bulgaria’s president can win in round one only if over half of all voters turn out
body: On 25 October 2026 Bulgaria voted for its president, and the race went to a runoff on 1 November, [AP reported](https://www.ajc.com/news/2026/10/presidential-race-in-bulgaria-heads-to-runoff-due-to-record-low-turnout/). Bulgaria’s [constitution](https://www.constituteproject.org/constitution/Bulgaria_2015) sets two conditions for a first-round win: a candidate needs more than half of the valid ballots, and more than half of all eligible voters must have cast a ballot. Miss either, and the two leading candidates meet again within seven days, where whoever gets more votes wins, however many people vote. In 2026 both conditions failed: among 27 pairs of candidates for president and vice-president, President Iliana Iotova and her running mate got about 35% and former caretaker prime minister Andrey Gyurov and his about 32%, while fewer than a quarter of the 6.6 million registered voters took part, a record low. A majority alone is not enough either: in 2006 President Georgi Parvanov won 64% in the first round, but turnout was 44%, so he faced a runoff, which he won with 76%.

slides.prompt: In Bulgaria’s 2006 presidential election, President Georgi Parvanov won 64% of the valid ballots in round one. Was he elected that day?
slides.answer: No: only 44% of voters turned out, so he faced a runoff.
slides.detail: Bulgaria’s constitution also requires more than half of all eligible voters to vote in round one. Parvanov won the runoff with 76%, on a turnout of 43%.

slides.alt: Animation on pine-green night: a ballot with 27 numbered pairs; a door marked win in round one with two padlocks, over half the ballots and over half the voters; 2026 bars of about 35% and 32% and a crowd of 100 with fewer than 25 voting; a runoff; 2006 with 64% on 44% turnout.

slides.prompt: Find a first round where the leader wins a majority of the ballots yet still faces a runoff, as in 2006.
slides.takeaway: Any share over 50% with a turnout of 50% or less does it: both conditions must hold. In 2006 Parvanov had 64% on a 44% turnout; the first round of 2026 failed both.

Over half of the valid ballots?

slides.heading: First round, 25 October 2026: share of the valid ballots
slides.note: Central Election Commission figures. Round one also needs over 50% turnout; it was under 25%.

slides.question: Under Bulgaria’s constitution, what turnout does the presidential runoff need for its winner to be elected?
slides.explanation: None: in the second round the candidate with more votes wins. The turnout rule applies only to winning in round one.
